Early in its history, the El Cerrito neighborhood consisted primarily of orange and lemon orchards and 19th century suburban development. Significant development began in the early 1920's when the old Cajon road became U.S. Highway 80 or "El Cajon Boulevard."Today, El Cerrito spans residences both north and south of El Cajon Blvd and is bordered by 54th/Collwood Street to the West; University Avenue to the South; College Avenue to the East; and Baja Canyon, south of Baja Drive, to the North. neighborhood_overview: East Village is a popular neighborhood in downtown San Diego.  A great place to enjoy all the excitement and convenience of Downtown living!  East Village is vibrant, creative and diverse.  A quick walk in any direction will take you to rooftop bars, restaurants, boutiques, galleries, live music venues, theaters and  luxury clubs.  Major attractions like Gaslamp District, Horton Plaza mall, Petco Park are only a 5-7 walk.  Seaport Village, the Convention Center, Midway Museum and The Museum of Contemporary Art are only a 10-15 walk.  Easy access to quick public transportation trips to the famous San Diego Zoo, Balboa Park, Old Town and more.  It is a perfect spot to start exploring beautiful San Diego.   Most of San Diego is only a 15-20 minute drive away such as La Jolla, Pacific Beach, Ocean Beach, Point Loma, Chula Vista and El Cajon. With a 10 drive you can get to Mission Valley, Fashion Valley, Old Town, Hillcrest, Southpark, Bankers Hills and North Park.
notes: The parking spot included in this listing is not guaranteed (available 99% of the time). Off site parking is metered but free with use of my handicap placard.  Noteworthy: be sure to pay attention to all posted signs and to the street sweeping nights and  “No Parking" hours.
transit: Just two blocks to bus routes and three blocks to trolleys.  Enterprise Auto Rental is very near.   Located just a few blocks from the 5, 163, and 94 freeways, most of San Diego is only a 10-15-20 minute drive. Local free rides are available (92101), just ask how.  Lyft and Uber drivers are usually quick to respond.
access: Everywhere but my room ;-)
interaction: Almost always home.  Spend a lot of time laying flat due to mobility issues, So while you get a lot of privacy, good conversation and a shared meal is always optional.

The area was developed by Matthew Sherman. Mr. Sherman was a developer in San Diego and created "Sherman's Addition," or "Sherman's Heights". He purchased the land in June 1867, a month after Alonzo Horton (Horton Plaza) purchased land for New Town San Diego (now downtown). Sherman Heights is the largest historic district in San Diego and features outstanding Victorian Architecture including the Villa Montezuma which is only a few blocks away from Parc Suites San Diego.

neighborhood_overview: SDhouse is located in the long established neighborhood Park West, an area which also acquired the name "Bankers Hill" because of its reputation as a home for the affluent. Bankers Hill is one of San Diego's nicest upscale residential neighborhoods located west of Balboa Park and east of Little Italy. Bankers Hill is best known for some of the grandest homes in San Diego and the incredible hillside view that looks over downtown San Diego and the Pacific Ocean. Banker's Hill has some of the best examples of high end residential architecture that dates back to the late 1800's. Examples of Victorian, Craftsman, Revival, and Emerging Modern homes can be seen throughout the Bankers Hill area. Many of the original mansions that were built here have been restored to their original beauty and some have been converted into professional buildings used by lawyers, doctors, dentists, and small companies. Just about 15 minutes from the house is Belmont Park, where you can ride roller coasters, go rock climbing, play a round of mini golf, and so much more. There's something for everyone at this historic San Diego park!  Make your way downtown for a once-in-a-lifetime tour of the USS Midway, a full-sized aircraft carrier docked in the harbor. After you're done, walk over to Seaport Village and browse the boutique shops before sitting down for a gourmet meal at one of the restaurants.  You can't visit San Diego without taking a day trip to Coronado Island. Cross the massive bridge and make a stop at Hotel Del Coronado, a historic luxury hotel located on a pristine beach.

Howdy Airbnb'ers!

Thank you for checking out our page! A little about me...I'm Amy and I live with my boyfriend Jade in San Diego, CA. We are a pretty chill couple who love to travel, stay active, cook/eat, and enjoy the good life in San Diego.  We have a beautiful little toddler that has changed our lives for the better :) We enjoy craft beers, kombucha, music, good food, and our dog. Probably a lot like you, we aspire to travel the world and experience all different cultures and people! We love to meet new people from around the world and learn about their travels, experiences, and culture and love when people are able to utilize our home for that purpose.

A little about our place:

We live in a tranquil 2 bedroom 2 bath Second Floor Condo in the magical neighborhood of University Heights. If you want relaxation in the best city on the West Coast, then you have found your destination!  We look forward to hosting you and assisting with making your trip to San Diego as comfortable as possible!

Our Sanctuary:

-Gated complex with apartment on second floor (staircase only)
- 2 private bedrooms with ceiling fans, master bedroom has attached full bath
- 2 queen size bed, bedding, towels, and sheets
-2 full baths 
-Plenty of Street Parking
-Wireless Internet
-Fully equipped and functioning kitchen with Gas burner oven
-Full size washer/dryer in unit

-Essential Oil Diffuser
-Large sectional couch that converts to a queen size sleeping area. 

Location:

-University Heights-Centrally located to everything in San Diego, close to public transportation, very walkable to cafes, bars, parks, shops and restaurants
-Bus stop is conveniently located right in the front of the complex; $2.25 one way, $5 day pass

Our home is discretely positioned in a small 12 unit condo complex near a bus stop with easy access to heart of University Heights, Normal Heights, Mission Valley, Downtown, Hillcrest, North Park, South Park,  and directly next to the Interstate 8 & 15.  The condo itself is very quiet with friendly neighbors.  Street parking available on Madison Ave, Arizona, or across the street behind gas station. You can bike to the beach if you can handle biking Texas St. ;)

Lastly, there are several good grocery stores near by: Sprouts, Trader Joes, Ralphs, Vons, and Whole Foods. Right down the hill is Mission Valley where there are several shopping centers, restaurants, and grocery stores. The airport, San Diego Zoo, Balboa Park, Downtown gaslamp district and shelter island, and beaches are minutes away from this central location in the city.

There are an unlimited number of fun bars, delicious eateries and coffee shops a short bike ride or long walk away.   Mission Bay, which is just 3 blocks away, is an incredible playground.  You can rent a boat or jet skis and pull them up to the park where you can setup a fun BBQ or bonfire.   There are dozens of miles of boardwalk and you can cruise the boardwalk checking out gorgeous coastline, stunning homes, stopping for food or drinks, etc, etc.   This is what the California lifestyle is all about!
transit: -it's about $15 to take a Lyft or Uber from the airport to the duplex.   -Once you're there you can ride the beach cruisers wherever you want to go in PB.  If you wish to check out other areas of San Diego: -La Jolla is the city north of Pacific Beach.  You can take an inexpensive Lyft or Uber to Birdrock or La Jolla Village then walk around and enjoy all that those areas have to offer. -Little Italy is the biggest hotspot in terms of restaurants right now and it's located between Downtown and the airport so it's also an inexpensive Lyft or Uber ride away.
access: This is unit 2 so you will have access to 2012 Reed Avenue, which is the back unit on the property.
interaction: My husband and I co-host your stay.  We live 6 blocks away and are just a call away if you need us.  If you are a group that prefers privacy and don't need us then you can certainly enjoy that since the front doors are setup with keypad locks so you can let yourselves in at any time.
house_rules: Small dogs are allowed for a total of 25 lbs or less.  For example, if you're bringing 1 dog it would have a 25 lb limit. If you're bringing 2 dogs they should be 25 lbs combined or less.  The front unit (2010 Reed Ave) has a fenced yard so that's the better unit for a dog.  San Diego has a “sound curfew,” or period of reduced allowable noise, between 11 p.m. and 8 a.m. on weekdays, and midnight to 9 a.m. or 10 a.m. on weekends.

My husband and I live in San Diego and we have a second home in South Florida that I purchased when I was commuting there for work .  We love to travel including snowboarding trips, beach destination trips and especially trips outside the US.

My husband Dave is American, works in biotech, is a wildlife enthusiast and a paraglider pilot. We have a large house and no kids so we are more than happy to share our spaces. We host a few AirBNB Experiences where we introduce our birds of prey to our guests and teach them to interact with them. We love it.

neighborhood_overview: Within a 5 minute walk you can reach most of the best restaurants, bars, and breweries in North Park. On a brewery tour? You can catch at least 6 different tasting rooms on one jaunt: Modern Times, Hess, Thorn Street, North Park Brewing, Belching Beaver, Fall Brewing to name a few.. We are happy to give suggestions!
notes: Please let us know in advance if there are any special accommodations you need. For instance, if you want to enjoy a bonfire outside or watch a movie on the outside projector please give us notice so we can arrange this for you. (Due to neighborhood quiet hours, you cannot be loud outside after 10:00PM.) The bikes are also easily accessible but please also give us heads up so we can have them ready for you in case the seats needs to be adjusted for you, tires need to be pumped, etc. We also have codes available for the bike and scooter rentals. We are recommending this option to guests that want to bike/scooter to a location but take different transportation back. Super convenient! And being parents to a young child, we are also baby friendly and let us know what you need to enjoy traveling with a youngster.
transit: We're about 6 blocks from the famous Balboa Park where you can catch the zoo, parks, museums, golf, and much more (It is a large park - the zoo is a short car ride or guests ride bikes there or a 40min walk). Heading downtown to Little Italy or Gaslamp? Catch a Lyft or Uber for about $10 and you're downtown in 10 minutes.  Beaches? 10-15 minute drive to major beaches such as Coronado, Pacific Beach, Ocean Beach, Point Loma... Busses? There is a major bus line only 2 blocks from the house. Bikes? Yes. We love bikes and encourage all guests to use them. We have vintage options for free or rent the city bikes/scooters and leave them anywhere.
access: Guests have access to their own cottage, laundry facilities, bikes, kitchenette, hot tub, hammocks, private patio, high-speed wireless internet, vintage record player with records, fireplace, and more. The cottage is small, but well-equipped. There's a first aid kit, hair dryer, toiletries, towels, french press coffee, and a lot more. The 'kitchenette' consists of a fridge, microwave, toaster, hot water heater... good for enjoying breakfast or heating up leftovers from all the restaurants you can walk to. There is NOT a cooktop with pots and pans so if you want a place with a full kitchen to cook all your meals, this is not the set up for you. If you need anything else just ask us and we'll get it for you!
interaction: Some guests we interact with a lot and spend a whole evening together. Others would just like to come and go and have more privacy. This is on your terms and also if we are around the same time you are. (Sometimes we might also be out of town during your stay, but we will always communicate this with you). Every interaction is unique! Feel free to reach out and talk to us or just mind your own... And never, EVER hesitate to let us know how we can improve your stay!
house_rules: All we ask is that you please be respectful of the property and the animals that live on it. The old plumbing is sensitive - please do not put anything other than bathroom tissue in the toilet. No smoking inside the cottage. You're welcome to smoke outside as long as you properly dispose. Lastly, when you are gone for extended period of time please turn the lights and A/C off in the cottage. Pets - No pets on the bed, cats are not allowed due to allergies from other guests. Dogs must be well-behaved and on a leash at all times when outside to protect our chickens. Please clean up after your dog.

Parking downtown can be a bit tricky/expensive (as with any city), but there are several free parking options right on our block or within a few blocks from our home. Just make sure to read the ordinances carefully as they change for different days. Just head east up Voltaire St and you’ll find coffee shops, local shops, bars and restaurants. The OB pier is a popular attraction for newcomers with the beautiful views of the coast and a hot spot for fishing. Newport Ave being the main street is just a 0.5-mile walk from the cottages offering a variety of locally owned restaurants, unique boutiques, antique shops, and microbreweries appealing to all. neighborhood_overview: Free parking on our road. A residential road that is a two minute walk to the hip International Restaurant row with some of San Diego's most popular restaurants such as Lucha Libre, as seen on Man vs Food, Shakespeare's pub and great coffee. Travelling the other direction takes you to Historic Old Town where you can find plenty of Mexican restaurants.

Please let us know when booking if this is a problem for you and we will make sure we don't take any animals in during your stay. Check in window- no one wants to be waiting around so please communicate in advance. Checkout is by 10.30am, but please discuss.
transit: Free access from airport, ask us how! We're an 8 minute walk from Washington Street Trolley Station running to Downtown/Convention Center and in the other direction into Old Town/Mission Valley/Qualcomm Stadium. 4 minutes walk from the no. 10 bus that runs from Old Town to Mission Hills/Hillcrest/North Park.  The Old Town Coaster Station is one stop away, we often walk to Old Town for more Mexican restaurants, which is about 15 minutes on foot.   If you are driving there is plenty of free street parking and we have easy access to the I-5/I-8.  Marine Corps Recruit Depot is a three or four minute drive if you're in town for a graduation.   The airport is about a $10 Uber ride away, though if we can accommodate your schedule we may be able to come pick you up ourselves, (no promises that we can manage that for all bookings though.)
access: You have the guest bedroom and bathroom. There is a table and chairs on the back patio that you can feel free to use as well for if you want to eat at the house. We ask that you not eat in the room. If you need hot water in the morning for tea or coffee please ask us, we'll be happy to provide a hot drink in the morning if we are up and around.  We will give you a wifi access code when you arrive.
interaction: We're excited to have guests, but we respect that you're here to see the sights and enjoy this great city.  If you have any questions please ask, we have a lot of advice on restaurants, shopping, riding the trolley, places to go, etc.  One of us will probably be around at any time, but unless you come looking for us you'll be fine in your comfortable room.  Please remember to discuss checkout time before you go to bed.
house_rules: - Check in time is from 2pm to 10pm, but please let us know your predicted arrival time. We will not wait up late. - Check out time before 10.30am. We need to know what time you're leaving BEFORE the morning so one of us is there to take the key back. - Loss of key ($25) or damage to the property will incur a charge.  - No extra guests allowed inside who have not booked though Airbnb. - Shoes off inside the front door please! - No messy food in the bedroom, you can use our back patio for takeouts. Please ask before using anything outside of your bedroom and bathroom. - No loitering or smoking outside the property, or our neighbor's. Go all the way to the street if you smoke. No drugs either. - You can read the books on the shelves while you're here but please respect them and don't take them out of the house.

neighborhood_overview: This is a nice, quiet, safe neighborhood. It's also absolutely beautiful! The bay is 100 feet from the house; the ocean is about 100 yards away (you can hear the ocean late at night, esp. at high tide). South Mission Beach is much more residential than the rest of Mission Beach, partly because it dead ends at the jetty - no through traffic means far less traffic here than the rest of Mission Beach; crossing the boulevard to get to the ocean is much easier and safer here!
notes: Alcohol and smoking are prohibited on beaches and boardwalks, and most public spaces.  The cottage is also a strictly non-smoking space, and no pets are allowed; additionally, absolutely NO PARTIES or loud gatherings are permitted. Occupancy is limited to 4 persons, including children; any exceptions must be agreed to in advance by hosts.
transit: The nearest bus stop is within walking distance; the buses generally run every 15 minutes and are new and clean. That said, we don't think the public transit here is very good or comprehensive. If you plan on just hanging out at the beach, you can get away with having no car; there are restaurants close by, a small market down the street, and you can also use the bikes at the cottage to get around. But, if you plan on doing sightseeing and going to a lot of the city's attractions, we highly recommend having a car.

I take great pride in offering you a home away from home which is clean, safe, private. and has what I hope includes everything you need to feel comfortable after a long day of touring San Diego. I can recommend the "must sees" for you to make the most of your visit, and hope that you will leave my city with fond memories, and anxious to return. I also offer you a money back guarantee, so that if you're not happy for any reason with your accommodations, I'll make sure you get a refund for any unused nights.  I love my day job working with kids who keep me grounded and young at heart. I have a great sense of humor,  and like to spend my weekends just relaxing at home with the Weber grill and some good company.  My mother used to tell me that you need only 3 things to be happy: Something to do, someone to love, and something to look forward to. Heeding her advice, I look forward to hosting you soon!  Happy travels, Filbert.

name: Enjoy North Park at Comfy & Chic Bungalow Retreat
summary: This thoughtfully decorated bungalow boosts high ceilings, natural sunlight & a spacious, open-concept floor plan. Explore breweries, restaurants  & boutique shopping nearby that are sure to give you a satisfying taste of the local San Diego scene!
space: We built our back house from the ground up.  All finishing touches are new and comfortable.  The bungalow is a comfortable 680 sq ft 1 bedroom home.  We live on site in the front house and are available if you need anything.  With your own alley parking and coded gate entry, you will have privacy.  Our backyard sits between both houses.  We do have children that enjoy playing in the yard but we are mindful when we have guests to assure you are not disturbed.  The lovely private outdoor space with the bungalow is fenced off from our yard and provides you a cozy outdoor area all to yourself.  It has a bbq grill and seating.  We are walking distance to two neighborhood markets, pizza, brewery, coffee shop, ice cream, and BBQ spot.  The brewery has a different food truck every evening of the week.  Lot's of options in just an 8 block walk thru a darling neighborhood.  And just a little further off within 12 blocks are so many more options!  We have a couple bikes we are happy to loan out.
description: This thoughtfully decorated bungalow boosts high ceilings, natural sunlight & a spacious, open-concept floor plan. Explore breweries, restaurants  & boutique shopping nearby that are sure to give you a satisfying taste of the local San Diego scene!
neighborhood_overview: From craft beers to coffee shops, North Park is sure to satisfy your taste buds!  A variety of local shops + restaurants=your hardest vacay decision...choosing which ones to visit! North Park is ranked third-hottest hipster neighborhood in America.
notes: This is not a party house.  We are a young family and like to have fun and want you to enjoy your vacation, but no loud disturbances and large groups.  No entertaining and late night shinanagins that will disturb our neighbors.  Families are welcome but the home is not suited for those with small children under 3 as it is not a child proof environment.
transit: nearest bus stop is 12 blocks away.  Bikes available upon request.  We suggest Uber for the most popular and cost effective way if you are in need of transportation.
access: You park in the alley and access the bungalow from the alley side gate.  This home is on the back end of our property which again is why it has alley access.  There are many homes along the alley on both sides as it is very common for double lots in San Diego to have a “back house”.  The alley is well lite at all times and we do have motion sensor lights around the property to light it well as you come and go when it is dark out.  Many other cars also park in the alley as it is the main access to the homes on the other side of the alley...meaning this alley way is well kept and acts as the front entrance to the houses across the alley. Just to paint a picture that it isn’t a creepy alley haha  The gate is coded for easy entry, as is the front door.  No keys necessary!  And to make it even easier...you get to choose the 4 digit code!
interaction: We aim to make your visit a fun and memorable experience.  It can be hard to arrive after a long day of travel to an unfamiliar place.  We are happy to stock the kitchen with your grocery list of requests.  In addition, if you are on a special trip and would like to add any surprises such as flowers or wine, we can also make that happen!  Such additional services will be invoiced separately.
house_rules: The home is not childproofed.  Please be mindful when traveling with little ones.  Please plan ahead so you can bring necessary items! We care about your kiddos also and understand how difficult it can be to travel with young children. Please let us know how we can help and don’t hesitate to reach out with any questions or concerns. The home is very clean we just do not supply outlet covers for example.
host_about: We are just soaking up the good times raising our family in sunny Southern California.  Central to all that San Diego has to offer, we love to explore our ever growing city and the many charming coastal towns north of San Diego.  From the beach to the zoo, we enjoy being outside and on an adventure.

neighborhood_overview: Jeremy & Alex’s home is located in San Diego, California, United States. Ocean Beach (also known as O.B.) is a beachfront neighborhood of San Diego, California. It has been called California's most authentic remaining beach town. Residents of Ocean Beach often refer to themselves as "OBceans" or "OBecians," which is pronounced "oh-BEE-shun" (although the proper spelling is a matter of dispute). The Ocean Beach Municipal Pier, built in 1966, is the longest concrete pier on the West Coast at 1,971 feet. The northern end of O.B.'s waterfront is known as Dog Beach. It's open 24 hours a day for leash-free dogs and was one of the first such beaches in the United States (founded in 1972). Ocean Beach and adjacent Point Loma are home to a sizable population of feral parrots and their offspring, known locally as the "O.B. air force." The sub-tropical climate is nearly ideal for parrots. The parrots, mostly Amazons, are most active and vocal at sunrise and sunset - Wiki :)

In order to use the reserved parking space, your vehicle must fit within the space length-wise, and not protrude into the alley which will block it and become a hazard to your vehicle and other drivers. host_about:
5 things I can't live without:
Love of family and friends
Ability to provide for those I care for and those that are in need
To make others laugh and to laugh! 
To have a purpose to be used in this world in even in the slightest ways
Last but not least, the love of Jesus that has been freely given.

My hopes as your host is to offer a refreshing, unique space-beachy, fun, clean, and of a nice decor. I have lived in Jamaica, Mexico and traveled to fun places such as Hawaii and the Keys,  I try to mix a little of each in my places. 

I am also all about comfortable beds! I don't care how expensive a place is the beds are what I find to be important! I usually have mattress toppers on the beds to make them super comfy but if you're the type who wants a firmer mattress, you can always remove them. I also invest in upscale pillows AKA (very comfortable), my linens are soft and not scratchy. I am known to have the home of coziness and fluff! Everything is soft and plush! I firmly believe the home should be the place of peace and solace! After stepping out most of your day in the rats race the place of your home should be your greatest environment of serenity and relaxation and that is what I set as my goals in each of my airbnbs.

I would say 80% of my guests have been some of the most lovely, kind and appreciative people I have met. I have had a couple odd experiences with some guests (which sort of make for good laughs-in time) but it's the ones who come in with an inspection clipboard that seem to be here to inspect rather than relax and enjoy life. Those guests have also challenged me to improve in those areas, so even when I get a "not so warm" review I try to use that to improve and offer even better services! What I do ask and truly welcome is when a guest checks in and if they find something less than desirable to please contact me ASAP and I will work my hardest to accommodate. I value your time, money and I want to be part of providing an atmosphere that you can truly enjoy. I want to know your concerns or needs "during your stay" not after reading a review, I know its easy to get shy and find it incomfrotable to make a complaint but I embrace any issue with gladness as it offers both of us a chance to make your stay the best it can be! So please upon arrival if something is not to your standard, or an item you may need not available (big or small) please contact me ASAP and we will be quick to rectify any situation.

My guests are important to me. Free to contact me anytime. Money doesn't come by easy and your trip is not free, and vacation time is even harder to get than money! So please stay in communication with me during your stay, I am always here for you!

One of my passions is travel: I've been fortunate to Scuba dive in the Red Sea, Palau, & Fiji, ski at Whistler, Breckenridge and Mammoth, cruise the Baltic, Mediterranean and meet friends for sun & fun in Sydney, Capetown and Thailand. 
I'm lived in and am a landscape designer in beautiful San Diego the past 24 years.

Hi there. I'm Bob. I'm  a 24 year old living in southern California and whilst I miss my friends and family back home, I absolutely love my new home here in San Diego! 

I enjoy traveling the world and creating new experiences. My favorite countries are Argentina, Croatia, Indonesia and Australia. Though these travels, I've been fortunate to learn what a good Airbnb experience (and host) looks like: A great home, with a friendly host, in an awesome neighborhood, and the ability to do the things you love! neighborhood_overview: Ocean Beach is located west of downtown San Diego. It still has the feel of a small Southern California beach town- laid-back, eclectic, a little eccentric and friendly. This beach community consists of predominantly smaller, independent business owners that provide a wide array of activities, great dining and shopping. The Wednesday Farmer’s Market, The OB Pier and Dog Beach are iconic to Ocean Beach.  It is also becoming home to many craft beer breweries. And it will always be the best place to try to count the most VW buses! The Sunset Cliff neighborhood consists mostly of residential homes and The Sunset Cliff Nature Park. Secluded Bermuda Beach is 1 block north of The Beachcliff Villas. The tide pools, the surf spots and the view make Sunset Cliffs a favorite spot for outdoor enthusiasts. Downtown San Diego and The Gaslamp District, the San Diego Airport, Point Loma Sportfishing, Old Town, Balboa Park and the Trolley Station are all within 15 minutes by car.  Route 35 Ocean Beach

I help people heal and recover and then go on to develop magical and meaningful lives and relationships. My wife and I are Marriage & Family Therapists. We have been ecstatically married for 40 years and have two beautiful daughters who have, as of late, given us three amazing grandchildren.

I also do Divorce Mediation, Collabrative Divorce—as a Coach and Child Specialist, Collabrative Wills, Trusts and Estates, and Dispute Resolution.

create a win/win friend relationships!!! I get great pleasure out of sharing my love of San Diego with visitors. Thank you for considering us to be your host!!

neighborhood_overview: South Park is one of San Diego's hidden gems. It's small enough to evoke a strong sense of community, but bustling with great restaurants, bars, shops, and more.  A quick 5 minute walk and you'll be in the heart of the neighborhood. We'll fill you in on some of our favorite spots.  If you're looking to turn it up a notch, the North Park neighborhood is nearby with great nightlife and microbrewery options.  Hillcrest and downtown San Diego/Gaslamp are also a cheap Uber/Lyft ride away. For those looking to enjoy the great outdoors, our place backs up to  Balboa Park. You'll enjoy easy access to hiking trails, the Balboa Park Golf Course, the Balboa Tennis Club, the Bud Kearns Memorial Swimming Pool, the San Diego Velodrome, and the Morley Field Disc Golf Course.  On the west side of the park, you'll find the world famous San Diego Zoo, the San Diego Natural History Museum, the San Diego Air & Space Museum, The Old Globe Theater, and much more. It's definitely worth exploring.

neighborhood_overview: From what we've heard, during ancient times Logan Heights was a rough neighborhood.  Instead now the neighborhood is blossoming & bustling with activity;  condos & renovations seem to be popping up every other week.   This is an authentic Mexican cultured neighborhood and it is delightful.  Children play soccer on the street, the neighbor on the corner sells tamales from their front yard every Friday and the line backs down the sidewalk.  Other neighbors grill and party to mariachi music on Fridays.  This is a neighborhood lush with life, its also a neighborhood that is lived in.  If you have a pulse you will enjoy this neighborhood. The people are great! If you are into urban art there are several galleries with 2x blocks walking distance.  The neighborhood holds weekly cultural events and is home to one of the most famous taco shops in San Diego (iSalud).
notes: There is ample street parking during most ocasions.  However, the house is situated across the street from a large church which hosts regular events, parking is limited during these events. neighborhood_overview: Rolando Village is a quiet, hidden neighborhood in San Diego’s Eastern Area. First laid out in the 1920s and built primarily in the postwar boom of the 1940s and 50s,  Rolando is home to the nostalgic architecture and beauty of close-knit, bungalow-style houses set in Eastern Area’s charming rolling hills. Many special features set Rolando Village apart. Take a walk on Rolando’s safe sidewalks in the evening to enjoy the warm yellow glow of our acorn-style lamp posts.  Explore our eight unique “catwalks” (public sidewalks in-between houses) which connect many of Rolando’s meandering, tree-lined streets.  Visit our burgeoning restaurant scene which boasts many award-winning destination spots like Garden Kitchen, Terra American Bistro, Bistro Sixty (San Diego Desserts), Next Door Wine Bar, Alforon Lebanese Cuisine, and much more.
notes: The guest suite stays very cool. If you don't like an air conditioned space that stays around 70 degrees than this may not be for you. You can always open windows to let warm air in, but you won't be able to control the thermostat since it's connected to the main house too.  We have a large dog (labradoodle), who we take out in the backyard to play during the day.  Please refrain from cooking with foods that have a strong smell, because cooking smells travel through the vents into the main house. Turn on the kitchen window fan when cooking to reduce smells and increase air circulation.

host_about:
Hi , my name is Leticia, born and raised in Los Angeles. I’ve been a local of San Diego for about 30 years. This is the first time I have lived so close to the Pacific Ocean and I love it!  Now I’m walking distance to Mission Bay and a bike ride to the beach. I love my neighborhood and feel completely safe living with just one young female roommate, Miranda, and my Labrador retriever, Izzy who is everything to me. If you stay at my place she will not bother you, but when you arrive she may bark and she does have a pretty  vicious bark , a wanna-be-watch dog,  but after she meets you she will be your new best friend, invite you in and probably show you where the valuables (Website hidden by Airbnb) other words she is super friendly, once she meets you. Plus she loves kids and playing with them. Not the watch dog I was hoping for; however, but she is my love.

 A little background.... i grew up in the San Fernando Valley (Los Angeles) , I attended the University Of Puget Sound in Tacoma, Washington, majoring in Elementary Education and Psychology !1983) I then moved to San Diego  and began teaching  school and figure skating. (I was a Competitive skater most of my childhood and teen years). I was married for a few years and have one son who is 22 years old and just graduated  USD 2018 and lives in San Diego.  He is my pride and joy along with Izzy who is 5.. I was blessed with this house in 2015.  Although I love living here I did not quite anticipate the costs of having a pool and more sq. ft. than I’m used to. So....I  realized I needed to generate some extra income being that I became a little overwhelmed with the upkeep and bills. Besides having a roommate, I decided to try Airbnb and  see how it would work out for me. I must say it is a very gratifying and wonderful experience! I have met tons of amazing people! I truly didn’t believe I would be good at hospitality or that this would be something I would like so much, but  during the past year and half I  have been so touched by  the reviews from my guests. They make me feel so good. I  hope you will feel the same way if you stay at my home. If you want to meet me and talk thats great but certainly not necessary as You can let yourself in and never be bothered. I do like to check in via text throughout your stay in regards to the temperature, if you need anything in particular, and when you like the hot tub turned on or to show you where certain things are that you might want to use. There are many nights that I do not stay upstairs due to another Airbnb that we are working on now and opens in November of 2018 which will have room for 9-10 people. 

My type of hosting is that I try to make everyone feel at home and offer as many things as possible. All age groups can enjoy something at my place, whether it’s swimming, hiking, biking, surfing, ping pong, bbq, the spa, outside TV watching with heat lamps and a fire pit, x-box, ninetendo and WII games, multiple toys for all ages, infant furniture..I.e play n pack, high chair, bath tub, swing,  baby books, coloring . Numerous games for adults as well, etc. 

I also have a small kitchen with tons of appliances. The BBQ has two gas burners and there is a  new new miniature oven that you can cook a pizza and other things in plus a small electric burner in the guest suite, The Family Fun house has a fully equipped kitchen and you can cook big meals if you want. there is also tons of fun appliances, popcorn maker, panini, snow cone, quesadilla, pastry makers and a Keurig machine with assorted coffees and teas and much more.

Overall Airbnb has been a wonderful adventure and I have been so fortunate to have the greatest guests imaginable from all over the world! It is a good feeling to offer my home to people who are traveling and want more than a hotel will provide. I have not had any major problems with anybody damaging  Anything serious or  disrespecting my neighbors. Those were my two main concerns getting started, especially my neighbors and respecting them with the noise level.  I have found that 98% of the guests treat my home as if it were their own. Very respectful. 

It was a year this past July and So far everything has been fantastic. There are a couple of things I need to update and fix and plan to in the near future. I would like to make one of my entrances handicap accessible because   one entrance is a rock path with sand stones obstructed a little by the A/C and some trash cans. But if someone is disabled or in a wheelchair, they can always enter in through the garage which  has a ramp at the doorway entering into the house and a few steps to the guest suite.
Additionally,  I have tons of electronic games but have never played any because I am not that tech savy...maybe one of you will show me how to hook up the xbox!???!

Well if you are reading all of this, and I appreciate you taking the time to do so,  I hope you will consider staying at one of my places and I can assure you a very comfortable and enjoyable vacation!  I’m very friendly and enjoy making others happy so my motto is "I aim to please"! I want you to go home feeling that your experience was  everything you expected and more. I want you to feel at home and help yourself to anything in the suite or home. So with that being said... Book your spot and I’ll see you soon!

host_about:
I'm originally from Huntington Beach, just a few hours up the coast, and settled here in San Diego when I bought my 1922 craftsman house in 2008. After college I spent about 7 years going to sea on commercial ships as a Marine Engineer, then worked as a shore side ship surveyor before finally landing my dream job here as a Port Engineer. My career has allowed me opportunity to travel all over the world for both work and pleasure; and while I still have an ambitious bucket list, I would love to go back to New Zealand, Bali, and Croatia to do some more exploring.
Despite all the places I've seen, San Diego is home, and I absolutely love living here. Most of my hobbies involve water in some form: surf, SCUBA, SUP (stand up paddle), and snowboarding. I hike frequently with my Mexicana rescue pup, Dewey, try new recipes on unsuspecting friends, test my amateur photography skills, and get bendy doing yoga to stay in surf-shape.
One of my favorite things to do is host friends and loved ones at my house, and make recommendations of things to do, places to go, etc. So I decided to join the airbnb family and expand my hosting horizons to meet more people and share the stoke. Happy happens in San Diego, and I look forward to meeting you and showing you some of the reasons why I love living here :)

neighborhood_overview: This neighborhood is a very safe and walkable neighborhood and has many restaurant choices.  When you Goog "South Park San Diego" it says:  "South Park is a charming residential area with popular neighborhood restaurants that range from innovative vegan food to upmarket Italian eats. Tree-lined Fern and 30th streets, the main thoroughfares, are also home to indie boutiques and cafes, while nearby Grape Street Dog Park has views over the downtown skyline. The adjacent Golden Hill area is known for its classic bungalow homes and artisanal coffee bars." The house is located exactly one mile to the center of South Park (a couple of good hills on the way if you want to walk, and only one hill if you head to North Park).   1.5 miles to many great North Park restaurants and 2 miles to many more. If you enjoy a walk or run or hike, there are many canyon trails that I walk almost every day. If you want to see the trails, they are all marked on Goog Maps when you switch from driving to walking.
notes: To respect my neighbors, quiet outside after 10 p.m. When you first arrive, if I am not home, there is a lock box on the front door.  That way you can come inside and make yourself at home.  I will be there the first time you meet my dog Marco.  If I'm not here when you arrive I will have Marco with me.   I can also keep him away from you the entire time you are here if you are uncomfortable with dogs in any way.  Marco gets along with all dogs, and if you bring your dog(s) (limit two), your pooch must not be aggressive or a repetitive barker.  It is not fair to me or my neighbors. There is a $25/night dog fee billed separately through Airbnb.
transit: Plenty of street parking.  You will usually be able to park right in front of the house.  My neighbors do not park in front of the house, but occasionally their guests do. Nearest bus stop is one mile.  Most people use a  bicycle or Uber or Lift, or the new scooters.

neighborhood_overview: Jeremy & Alex’s home is located in San Diego, California, United States. Ocean Beach (also known as O.B.) is a beachfront neighborhood of San Diego, California. It has been called California's most authentic remaining beach town. Residents of Ocean Beach often refer to themselves as "OBceans" or "OBecians," which is pronounced "oh-BEE-shun" (although the proper spelling is a matter of dispute). The Ocean Beach Municipal Pier, built in 1966, is the longest concrete pier on the West Coast at 1,971 feet. The northern end of O.B.'s waterfront is known as Dog Beach. neighborhood_overview: While some may compare San Diego’s Mission Beach to the East Coast’s Atlantic City and Coney Island, there is a unique Southern California vibe you can’t find anywhere else here. Nestled between Pacific Beach on the north side, and Belmont Park on its southern side, Mission Beach offers a lively and robust variety of activities in the sun, surf and sand. From hot dog stands to fine dining eateries, hot night clubs to street performers, expect to find all kinds of free-spirited beach goers in a fun, carnival-like atmosphere along the sandy shores. Mission Beach is a community built on a sandbar between the Pacific Ocean and Mission Bay. It is part of the city of San Diego, California. Mission Beach spans nearly two miles of ocean front.  Most of the action in Mission Beach centers around Belmont Park at the intersection of Mission Blvd. and West Mission Bay Drive where you can ride the historic Giant Dipper roller coaster, or rent a set of rollerblades to ride up and down the boardwalk.
notes: Walking/running paths on both the beach side and the bay side.   Supermarket within walking distance, also nearby farmers' markets in summer. host_about:
Hi! I'm Teresa. I'm 29, and I live in San Diego, CA. I'm originally from Albuquerque, NM. I'm obsessed with chips, Taco Bell, The Office, and my pug, Charlie. I'm a full-time barber, in San Diego's vibrant Hillcrest neighborhood. Working as a barber means I get to meet and chitchat with people from all walks of life -- it's great that I get to meet so many different people each day! 

Working on my succulent garden is one of my favorite hobbies!  I enjoy going to baseball games, wandering around the city, visiting the various swap meets around town, and people watching (I do live downtown!). I also enjoy traveling, and would love to visit Thailand someday. I really love true crime stories; I think I was a homicide detective in a past life!

New York City and San Francisco are among my favorite travel destinations. I'd love to explore the east coast, and visit Washington, D.C. in particular. Visiting the Smithsonian (with enough time to fully explore it) would be a dream. 

I love to meet new people, and I look foward to meeting you, whether as a guest or a host!

host_about:
5 things I can't live without:
Love of family and friends
Ability to provide for those I care for and those that are in need
To make others laugh and to laugh! 
To have a purpose to be used in this world in even in the slightest ways
Last but not least, the love of Jesus that has been freely given.

My hopes as your host is to offer a refreshing, unique space-beachy, fun, clean, and of a nice decor. I have lived in Jamaica, Mexico and traveled to fun places such as Hawaii and the Keys,  I try to mix a little of each in my places. 

I am also all about comfortable beds! I don't care how expensive a place is the beds are what I find to be important! I usually have mattress toppers on the beds to make them super comfy but if you're the type who wants a firmer mattress, you can always remove them. I also invest in upscale pillows AKA (very comfortable), my linens are soft and not scratchy. I am known to have the home of coziness and fluff! Everything is soft and plush! I firmly believe the home should be the place of peace and solace! After stepping out most of your day in the rats race the place of your home should be your greatest environment of serenity and relaxation and that is what I set as my goals in each of my airbnbs.

I would say 80% of my guests have been some of the most lovely, kind and appreciative people I have met. I have had a couple odd experiences with some guests (which sort of make for good laughs-in time) but it's the ones who come in with an inspection clipboard that seem to be here to inspect rather than relax and enjoy life. Those guests have also challenged me to improve in those areas, so even when I get a "not so warm" review I try to use that to improve and offer even better services! What I do ask and truly welcome is when a guest checks in and if they find something less than desirable to please contact me ASAP and I will work my hardest to accommodate. I value your time, money and I want to be part of providing an atmosphere that you can truly enjoy. I want to know your concerns or needs "during your stay" not after reading a review, I know its easy to get shy and find it incomfrotable to make a complaint but I embrace any issue with gladness as it offers both of us a chance to make your stay the best it can be! So please upon arrival if something is not to your standard, or an item you may need not available (big or small) please contact me ASAP and we will be quick to rectify any situation.

My guests are important to me. Free to contact me anytime. Money doesn't come by easy and your trip is not free, and vacation time is even harder to get than money! So please stay in communication with me during your stay, I am always here for you!

My husband is a pharmacist so he volunteers at our health outreaches on his weekends off.

I have a broker license so I work at my parent’s real estate investment company.  I help purchase, manage and/or flip properties which can be stressful. Five things that I cannot live without is family, friends, travel, books, and good food.  I am a big foodie—I love to try new dishes and explore various restaurants and cuisines, especially when I’m traveling.  My favorite travel destination is Japan, Spain and Costa Rica.  My favorite book is Jane Austen.  My favorite music are oldies.  And my favorite food is sushi.

As a guest, I am very courteous and considerate.  I will follow the house rules to the tee and make sure that he house is clean.  Since I am also a host, I understand how important it is to treat the rental well and be respectful as a guest.  

As a host, I am friendly, nice and accommodating.  I live down the street from my rental so I am available and can provide assistance if needed.  

 My two motto is: “Life is short so enjoy every moment of it” and “Treat other people how you want to be treated:  with kindness”

neighborhood_overview: The cottage is located in the beautiful neighborhood of South Park. Two blocks from the cottage are a couple of shops, a fantastic deli (Grant's), Hamilton's bar, The South Park Brewing Company, Kindred (Vegan) and Buona Forchetta restaurants. About a mile walk is the heart of South Park with boutique shops, a great burger place (The Station), and numerous other restaurants and bars. The Big Kitchen is a breakfast and lunch place where Whoopie Goldberg got her start as a dishwasher. In the fall of 2018 we will be welcoming three new restaurants-Indian food, breakfast and lunch restaurant and a sports bar. Check out (Website hidden by Airbnb) for a list of all restaurants, bars and shops within walking distance. The majority of the homes in South Park are over 100 years old and most are in the Craftsman style of architecture. You will find historically registered homes on nearly every street in this small neighborhood.  It's a great walking neighborhood.
notes: Just ask if you need anything else.  I've been accused of being an over-sharer. You can take the Okie out of Oklahoma but...
transit: There is plenty of street parking available in front of the house and we also do not have street sweepers so you don't have to worry about moving your car. A short bike ride or car ride and you are able to be in North Park, Balboa Park, or downtown San Diego. (Bikes and Bird electric scooters can be rented throughout South Park) and in about a 15 minute car ride our beautiful beaches are at your disposal! The cottage is located two blocks from the major bus route and is only about a $15.00 cab ride from the airport. There is also a large amount of Lyft and Uber cars available if you are familiar with those options as well.
access: While the cottage opens up to the backyard this is a shared space between the main house and another small gold guest house across the backyard where my niece Kate lives. Our guests are welcome to use this space as much as they would like, however please know you will see us coming and going through here and please be respectful of quiet hours 11pm to 9 am. There is a hot tub on the property but due to its location (next to the main house's master bedroom) the hot tub is off limits to the cottage guests. Sorry! I do have beach towels and beach chairs I would be happy to let you borrow for enjoying what San Diego is most famous for!  Just ask.

We will also not bother you.  If we are having a family or friend get together outside, I will always let you know beforehand and invite you to join us!

But mostly enjoy San Diego! Ask questions and for recommendations--I have lived here for over 12 years (when the only restaurant was a taco shop.)  I'm always willing to discuss some of my favorite places! Not only am I a homeowner in South Park.  I am also a business owner in South Park so I know the area.

"People never regret things that the DID do...only what they never did" 


Hi, I'm Joy..I live in the main house with my teenage daughter and our two Goldendoodle's- Sunshine and our new puppy Keegan. (The cottage is in the backyard.) I work most days as a psychologist in my private practice in South Park and two days a week I work with military dependents in a school setting.  When I'm not working I love being a mom, working in my garden, playing tennis and going to the gym while dreaming about my next travel adventure!  I love meeting people and have often been accused of speaking to every person that I pass on the street.  We have hosted foreign exchange students for the past 14 years and have made several trips to Europe to visit some of them.  I am from Oklahoma and have been raised to show my Southern hospitality so I hope you enjoy my cottage.

neighborhood_overview: OB is just the best! It is an 'attitude not an address' :) We live on such a great street... Voltaire! Our neighbors are super friendly and just all around cool Obeacians.  Everything you could want is either a walk or bike-ride away! Dog beach is literally at the end of the road, such an easy & fun walk. There are 2 yoga studios on Voltaire St. along with restaurants (2 of which are vegetarian/vegan), grocery stores (1 of which is an organic co-op), brewery and bars, cafes and coffee stands, and surfboard rental/repair shop. These businesses are all on Voltaire St., but not right next door. The neighbors are homes, not businesses. The cottage is surrounded by cool neighbors, but with easy access to all of the good stuff!
notes: Street sweeping in front of house every Friday & across the street every Wednesday. You can park in driveway. If you have multiple vehicles & park on street, please move your car to the appropriate side from the hours of 7:30-10:30am, otherwise you will likely be ticketed :( All of Ocean Beach & Point Loma are very close to the San Diego Airport ... it is the closest beach town to the airport, which makes it very convenient for travel, but unfortunately the planes can take some getting used to. The airport regulates travel, so there are no planes between hours of 10pm & 6am. If people are outside chatting, they wait a minute - its called the Point Loma Pause :) It is not a problem for us, but we had a renter who had a hard time, so I wanted to share as a FYI. Our home is just about a 10 minute drive to/from airport, but the plane sounds are not just at our house, rather all of Ocean Beach & Point Loma, so maybe wise to choose a different area of San Diego if you are sensitive to noise.

However, the main strip of bars and restaurants is only a short 4 blocks north if you want to get your party on. Mission Bay is visible from the end of our alley, and is an easy 2 blocks away to Fanuel Park. The bay is an ideal place for laying out, paddle boarding, swimming, and kayaking. Mission bay has a bike path that circumnavigates almost the entire bay. This is a great place to get out for an evening stroll by foot or bike. We can recommend lots of great restaurants, bar, and coffee shops depending on what you like. Some of our favorites include: Crown Point Coffee, Tap Room, and Vallarta.

neighborhood_overview: University Heights is a "pocket" neighborhood with North Park, Hillcrest, Normal Heights, Balboa Park, Bankers Hill and Mission Hills in close proximity.  During your walk to the pedestrian bridge you will encounter friendly neighbors as you stroll past architectural examples of the iconic "California Bungalow". The studio sits atop a ridge overlooking historic Route #163 and Mission Valley in the distance.   We are about 700 feet above the freeway and about 1/2 mile away. There is a distant hum of traffic from the freeway  so if you like complete silence, perhaps this isn't your best choice.  But if you want a quiet, walkable  neighborhood  close to the action, this is a great place.

Check out the Hillcrest Sunday Farmer's Market, voted the best in San Diego! Listen to live music while sampling yummy local and organic produce! Food booths to delight the senses. We have beach cruisers,  beach chairs, bocci and petanque balls to loan.
transit: Walking:  Everything you could want is within walking distance of a few blocks. City buses and Deca Bike Rentals are available after crossing the pedestrian bridge.
